risks: We derive significant portion of our revenues from projects awarded by government and government-owned customers, accounting for 27.57%, 56.43%, 69.66% and 62.90% of our revenue from operations during the period ended September 30, 2025, Fiscal 2025, Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2023, respectively, which subjects us to various risks.

Our dependence on government and government-owned customers therefore exposes us to risks relating to policy uncertainty, delays in project award, cost overruns, payment delays, and onerous contractual terms.
Expansion into other states may require us to establish new client relationships, comply with differing regulatory frameworks and compete with entrenched regional players.

Projects included in our order book may be delayed, modified, put on hold, cancelled, or not fully paid for by customers due to factors beyond our control, including funding constraints, customer defaults, delayed approvals, regulatory issues, changes in project priorities, adverse macro-economic conditions, supply chain disruptions, and force majeure events.
In addition, a significant portion of our projects are with government and public-sector clients, where contracts are awarded through competitive tendering.

However, certain projects have experienced execution-related delays, scope modifications, or extended timelines due to factors such as delayed approvals, site readiness issues, or administrative reasons, which are customary in EPC contracts, particularly those involving government or public-sector clients.

A substantial portion of our revenue, being 21.26%, 47.13%, 60.46% and 36.91% during the period ended September 30, 2025, Fiscal 2025, Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2023, respectively, is derived from railway infrastructure projects, and any slowdown, disruption, or adverse development in this sector could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
A substantial part of our revenue is concentrated from railway infrastructure projects.

other_material_facts.value: India’ Railway EPC Market Size Analysis, FY20–FY30F Between FY20 and FY25, the Railway EPC market increased from INR 16.2 thousand crore to INR 30.4 thousand crore, at a CAGR of 13.4%.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence

overview.business_overview:
We are an Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning (“EPCC”) company engaged in providing integrated infrastructure solutions across multiple domains, with a primary focus on the railway infrastructure, power transmission & distribution, and water & wastewater treatment sectors. Our expertise spans the entire project lifecycle design, engineering, procurement, erection, testing, commissioning, and operation & maintenance (“O&M”). We also operate an in-house manufacturing facility for High-Tension (“HT”) and Low-Tension (“LT”) electrical panels and compact substations, enabling us to offer customized, reliable, and cost-efficient products that complement our EPCC activities. We also undertake sub-contracting assignments, providing on-ground execution support for a wide range of engineering projects.

India’s EPC industry delivers services including design and engineering, procurement, civil works, installation, commissioning and operation and maintenance covering Railway EPC, Drinking Water & Wastewater Treatment, Power Distribution Panels and Compact Substation, Transmission and Distribution and SCADA and Automation. India’s Railway EPC market grew from INR 16.2 thousand crore in FY 20 to INR 30.4 thousand crore in FY 25 and is expected to reach INR 50.5 thousand crore by FY 30F. The drinking water and wastewater market is projected to reach INR 169.6 thousand crore by FY 30F, supported by growth across panels, transmission and distribution and SCADA segments. Indian Infrastructure EPC Market is defined as the total domestic revenue generated from engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) activities undertaken within India across Railway Infrastructure and Water Infrastructure segments, along with the related markets for HT/LT Power Distribution Panels, Compact Substations (CSS), and SCADA &

Automation Systems. (Source: Ken Report)

We operate through five interlinked business segments, each contributing to our integrated infrastructure and engineering solutions framework. Incorporated with the vision of delivering technically robust and cost-effective engineering solutions, we offer end-to-end project execution capabilities covering design, engineering, procurement, project management, construction, installation, testing and commissioning.

Our diversified business verticals include:

(a) Railway Electrification & Infrastructure:

Railway Electrification (RE) – We undertake RE and allied infrastructure works represent one of our principal business segments. We undertake EPCC projects involving the design, supply, erection, testing and commissioning of 25 kV AC Overhead Electrification (“OHE”) systems, Traction Sub-stations (“TSS”), and Sectioning and Paralleling Posts (“SP/SSP”). Our scope also includes associated civil works such as foundations, trenches, control room buildings, and ancillary structures, as well as signalling and telecommunication interface works. We execute projects for zonal railways, public sector undertakings, and large infrastructure contractors. The Company’s technical proficiency and adherence to RDSO standards enable efficient, safe, and reliable electrification execution.

Railway Infrastructure Works – Our company does composite nature of work involving civil, electrical, and mechanical works as part of the Railway Station Redevelopment with allied works and modernization programs initiated by Indian Railways under the “Amrit Bharat Station Scheme” and other national initiatives. Our services in this domain cover structural rehabilitation, construction of passenger amenities, illumination systems, internal and external electrification, foot over bridges, water supply and drainage systems, digital LED signages and integration of automation for energy management. Through these works, we contribute to the modernization of passenger interface infrastructure and enhancement of service standards across the Indian Railways network.

Indian Infrastructure EPC Market is defined as the total domestic revenue generated from engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) activities undertaken within India across Railway Infrastructure and Water Infrastructure segments, along with the related markets for HT/LT Power Distribution Panels, Compact Substations (CSS), and SCADA &

Automation Systems. (Source: Ken Report)

The Railway EPC Market is defined as the domestic revenue generated from EPC contracting activities related to railway electrification, signaling & telecommunication, and civil works in India. Between FY 20 and FY 25, the Railway EPC market increased from INR 16.2 thousand crore to INR 30.4 thousand crore, at a CAGR of 13.4%. From FY 25 to FY 30F, the market is expected to grow to INR 50.5 thousand crore, at a CAGR of 10.7%. (Source: Ken Report) In FY 25, India’s Railway EPC market on segmentation by work type, composite infrastructure works, accounted for 51.0%, followed by Electrification of Railway Lines at 13.8%, S&T Works at 12.8%, PEB for Sheds, Warehouses & Depots at 9.9%, OHE at 5.6%, Traction Substations at 4.3% and Power Transmission & Distribution Networks at 2.6%. Opportunities for EPC players lie in the execution of electrification, signaling, and station redevelopment works under flagship programs such as PM Gati Shakti, Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, and Mission Electrification. In addition, high-speed rail corridors, dedicated freight lines, and multimodal logistics hubs are creating sustained EPC demand across civil

The India Metro Systems EPC Market is defined as the domestic revenue generated from EPC contracting activities related exclusively to urban metro rail systems in India. India’s metro EPC market has grown steadily from ₹15,000 crore in FY 19 to an estimated ₹23,500 crore in FY 25, reflecting a CAGR of 7.8%, and is projected to reach ₹34,700 crore by FY 30F, reflecting an 8.1% CAGR (FY 25 – FY 30F). (Source: Ken Report) (b) Extra High Tension (“EHT”) Transmission and Distribution Systems:

Our company undertakes turnkey projects in Extra High Tension Transmission and Distribution Systems, covering voltage levels up to 220 kV. Its scope includes sub-station construction, installation of power transformers, switchgear, control and relay panels, busbar systems, and distribution networks. We also execute transmission line projects, including foundation works, tower erection, conductor stringing, and OPGW (“Optical Ground Wire”) integration. Our work in this vertical supports utilities, public sector undertakings, and industrial clients in strengthening grid reliability and power distribution efficiency. Its participation aligns with national programs such as the “Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) and Green Energy Corridors”, emphasizing grid modernization and renewable integration.

The Transmission and Distribution (T&D) Market is defined as the domestic EPC revenue generated from the design, supply, construction, and commissioning of transmission lines, substations, and distribution networks across India. As of FY 25, India’s transmission and distribution market size stood at INR 36,000.0 crore, growing at a strong CAGR of 16.2 % over FY 20 – FY 25. The market is projected to reach INR 60,063.0 crore by FY 30F, at a CAGR of 10.8 % (FY 25 –

In FY 25, India’s Transmission and Distribution Market Segmentation (INR ‘000 crore) by End User, state segment accounted for 66.1%, followed by Central segment at 21.9% and Private segment at 11.9%.Opportunities for EPC players lie in grid expansion, substation construction, feeder modernization driven by government programs such as the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), Green Energy Corridor, and National Electricity Plan, large-scale push for renewable evacuation and interregional transmission corridors and growing need for reliable power transmission to support water, industrial, and renewable infrastructure. (Source: Ken Report) (c) Water and Wastewater Treatment EPCC:

We provide turnkey EPCC solutions for Water Treatment Plants (“WTP”), Sewage Treatment Plants (“STP”), and Effluent Treatment Plants (“ETP”), along with associated civil, mechanical, and electrical works. Its capabilities cover intake wells, pumping stations, rising mains, pipelines, and process automation systems. The Drinking Water and Waste Water Treatment Market is defined as the domestic EPC revenue generated from the design, supply, and execution of drinking water treatment plants, wastewater/sewage treatment plants, distribution networks, pumping stations, and electro-mechanical works in India. India’s drinking water and wastewater treatment market expanded from INR 60.5 thousand crore in FY 20 to INR 99.9 thousand crore in FY 25, at a CAGR of 10.6%. It is expected to reach INR 169.6 thousand crore by FY 30F at a CAGR of ~11.2% (FY 25 – FY 30F). (d) Automation and SCADA Systems:

Automation and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (“SCADA”) solutions form an integral part of our service offerings. We design and implement Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)-based automation systems, RTU and HMI integration, instrumentation, control panels, and communication networks for remote monitoring and control of infrastructure assets. Our automation services are applied across its core business sectors railway electrification, water systems, and power distribution enhancing system reliability, efficiency, and operational safety.

The SCADA & Automation Systems Market is defined as the domestic revenue generated from the design, supply, execution, and commissioning of SCADA and automation systems across electrical networks, water and wastewater infrastructure, power projects, and railway installations in India. The Indian SCADA and Automation Systems market has grown from INR 5.1 thousand crore in FY 20 to INR 7.7 thousand crore in FY 25, reflecting a CAGR of 8.6%. The market projected to reach INR 12.0 thousand crore by FY 30F, registering a CAGR of 9.3% between FY 25 – FY 30F. (Source:

In FY 25, India’s SCADA and Automation Systems Market Segmentation by Application, Power Distribution SCADA accounted for 24.7%, followed by Oil & Gas SCADA at 23.4%, Other Applications SCADA at 16.9%, Manufacturing SCADA at 15.6%, Water Supply SCADA at 10.4% and Waste Water SCADA at 9.1%. (Source: Ken Report) The market offers growing opportunities for EPC players in deployment and integration of SCADA systems across power, water, and industrial assets. With utilities adopting IoT, cloud, and AI-based analytics, EPCs with automation capabilities can capture value in grid modernization, renewable integration, and smart water networks, supported by government-led digitalization programs driving steady automation-linked EPC demand. (Source: Ken Report) (e) Composite supply of HT/LT Distribution Panels along with related services:

We manufacture a wide range of High Tension (HT) and Low Tension (LT) distribution and control panels, including VCB panels, PCC, MCC, APFC, synchronization panels, and PLC-based automation panels. All panels are designed and fabricated in accordance with IS/IEC standards, ensuring safety, reliability, and consistent performance. Our in-house capability supports complete vertical integration from design and fabrication to assembly and testing allowing us to maintain strict quality control, optimize costs, and ensure timely delivery. In addition to meeting internal project requirements, this division also contributes to external revenue by supplying panels to third-party clients across industrial and infrastructure sectors. These panels are typically provided as a composite supply along with our installation, testing and commissioning services as part of our integrated project execution.

A major strength of this division is our capability to produce Compact Substations (CSS) with capacities up to 2.5 MVA and voltage levels up to 11 kV. These factory-built, fully integrated substations combine a transformer, HT panel, LT panel, and protection systems within a single compact enclosure. Their modular design, enhanced safety features, and reduced installation footprint make them ideal for industrial, commercial, and utility applications. This product segment represents a key differentiator for us, offering clients faster deployment, improved reliability, and lower lifecycle costs. We began our operations as a partnership firm in 2014 and were converted into a private limited company in 2022 under the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013. Headquartered in Mysore, Karnataka, we started as an EPC contractor and gradually expanded into a diversified infrastructure and utility solutions provider with integrated capabilities across design, engineering, installation, testing, commissioning, and O&M. Over the years, we have built relationships with government organizations, PSUs, utilities, and private enterprises across India. Our structure allows us to leverage synergies between our EPC and manufacturing divisions, enabling us to deliver end-to-end, technology-driven, and cost-optimized infrastructure solutions across sectors. Our business is supported by a Board of Directors with diverse functional and sectoral experience, providing strategic direction and oversight to the Company’s operations. The Board comprises Agrahara Chamaraje Gowda Abhinandan, Promoter and Managing Director, with over eleven years of experience in EPC, railway infrastructure, SCADA/automation, transmission and distribution and utility projects; Mahadevappa Tejus, Promoter and Whole-time Director, with over nine years of experience in project execution, procurement and construction management; and Hosahalli Appagigowda Savitha, Promoter, Chairman and Executive Director, with over seven years of experience in administration, governance and operational management. The Board also includes Anala, Promoter and Non-Executive Director, with engineering and industry experience in human resources and organizational development; Kikkeri Putte Gowda Jayaramu, Independent Director, with over thirty-four years of experience in urban infrastructure, water supply and sanitation projects; and Mysore Govindaraju Yashwanthkumar, Independent Director, with over nine years of experience in finance, accounting and taxation. The collective expertise of the Board supports informed decision-making, effective oversight of operations, and adherence to governance and compliance requirements.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- We derive significant portion of our revenues from projects awarded by government and government-owned customers, accounting for 27.57%, 56.43%, 69.66% and 62.90% of our revenue from operations during the period ended September 30, 2025, Fiscal 2025, Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2023, respectively, which subjects us to various risks.
- Our dependence on government and government-owned customers therefore exposes us to risks relating to policy uncertainty, delays in project award, cost overruns, payment delays, and onerous contractual terms.
- Expansion into other states may require us to establish new client relationships, comply with differing regulatory frameworks and compete with entrenched regional players.
- Projects included in our order book may be delayed, modified, put on hold, cancelled, or not fully paid for by customers due to factors beyond our control, including funding constraints, customer defaults, delayed approvals, regulatory issues, changes in project priorities, adverse macro-economic conditions, supply chain disruptions, and force majeure events.
- In addition, a significant portion of our projects are with government and public-sector clients, where contracts are awarded through competitive tendering.
- However, certain projects have experienced execution-related delays, scope modifications, or extended timelines due to factors such as delayed approvals, site readiness issues, or administrative reasons, which are customary in EPC contracts, particularly those involving government or public-sector clients.
- A substantial portion of our revenue, being 21.26%, 47.13%, 60.46% and 36.91% during the period ended September 30, 2025, Fiscal 2025, Fiscal 2024 and Fiscal 2023, respectively, is derived from railway infrastructure projects, and any slowdown, disruption, or adverse development in this sector could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
- A substantial part of our revenue is concentrated from railway infrastructure projects.
